scenario: [LCYC.3.1.1]: an SCC is refused when it consumes what it writes to the cache. Rule `r` matches a `Trig` whose `where` reads `cached("k")`, writes `cache key: "k"`, and withdraws its match, so `withdraw t` makes it a one-rule SCC through its own withdraw edge ([LCYC.3.2.2]). No schema is emitted, so the first condition holds; but a rule of the SCC writes key `k` and a rule of it reads `cached("k")`, so the SCC consumes what the cache holds and is refused with DS_VALIDATE_RULE_CYCLE. PATH PINNED: `dsc.cycle.lcyc_3_1_1_consumes_cache`, the write from `cache_writes_of` and the `where` read from `cache_reads_of`. Twin: LCYC.3.1.1_scc_writes_cache_unread_admitted, which drops the read and compiles.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope explicit:
    v: Int

rule r:
    Trig t where cached("k") != t.v
->
    cache key: "k" value: t.v
    withdraw t
